cases.identity: 1979 Evelyn 'Champagne' King music-video production rushes (Bristol Productions, New York), digitized by XFR Collective from Mark Pines' Umatic collection, organized by scene and take — a coherent multi-take shoot from which an editor selects the most effective shots of each scene and assembles them into a continuous sequence.
missing_information: No explicit license/rights field is recorded on the items or the markpines collection (collections: markpines, folksoundomy; some items also list xfrcollective). Reuse rights cannot be certified from the metadata alone; provenance is stated only as Umatic digitization via XFR Collective equipment loan from Mark Pines' collection.

No shot-level log, clapperboard slate metadata, or take-level timecodes are published; the association of each reel with its scene/take numbers comes solely from item titles, so exact in-reel take boundaries must be established by inspecting the footage.
No directorial/editorial brief (i2) exists in these records — that is a task_instruction input supplied later, not found here.

The 712×480 H.264 MP4s are lossy derivatives of 720×486 8–10 GB Cinepak AVIs; whether the derivative resolution/temporal quality is sufficient for fine performance/composition judgments is unverified without playback (native AVI originals are also downloadable if needed).

Relationship between the multiple reel dates (1979-03-27/28/29 and 1979-05-27, plus a Reel 14 titled 1978-03-28) and a single final cut is not documented; some reels may belong to different edits/versions of the same song.

stop_reason: A single coherent, case-bearing original-record set was located and verified: the 1979 Evelyn 'Champagne' King shoot rushes preserved by XFR Collective/Mark Pines on the Internet Archive, explicitly organized by scene and take across multiple reels (Scene 2 takes 1–4; Scene 3 takes 4–5; Scene 6 takes 7–15; Scene 7 takes 16–28; Scene 8 tape 37–38; Scene 9 takes 39–46). Each selected item has a confirmed native H.264 MP4 derivative (~80–132 MB, 712×480) plus the original multi-GB AVI, directly supporting node i1 (raw multi-take footage per scene) and, by extension, professional judgment i3 (take selection) and i4 (cross-scene ordering) leading to out1. Eight MP4 derivatives were selected within the total_selected_files limit, spanning scenes from earliest (Scene 2) to latest (Scene 9) so a full narrative can be assembled. The download URLs are canonical archive.org/download/<identifier>/<filename> paths that 302-redirect to content nodes (file presence confirmed; a node fetch returned real video data over the tool's size cap). No explicit license is recorded, so reuse rights are handed off as an open uncertainty rather than certified. Remaining gaps (take boundaries within reels, derivative resolution adequacy, relationship among the different shoot dates) are documented as missing_information and do not prevent independent inspection.
